extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A curated evaluation suite of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform average human-rater performance. The paper studies whether chain-of-thought prompting improves performance on these tasks and analyzes scaling behavior across models.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper analyzes BIG-Bench tasks, selects a subset of 23 particularly challenging tasks, and manually writes chain-of-thought exemplars for BBH.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: BIG-Bench tasks / evaluation suite, specifically a subset of 23 challenging tasks used to form BIG-Bench Hard (BBH).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some BBH tasks rely on factual and general knowledge about the world and on "common practices and presuppositions in the Western society," indicating a Western-society bias in task content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are limited by their dependence on specific world knowledge and cultural assumptions; performance can be worse on tasks like Causal Judgement and Ruin Names, and none of the language models outperform average human-rater performance on those tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The discussion notes that some tasks involve sarcasm detection, name disambiguation, entity resolution, and knowledge of Western cultural practices, implying that model performance may reflect or reinforce culturally situated language understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for evaluating model performance on BBH tasks, especially with Chain-of-Thought prompting, across reasoning and language-understanding categories; the discussion implies use for testing/benchmarking rather than training.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We select a subset of 23 particularly challenging tasks and group them into an evaluation suite referred to as BIG-Bench Hard (BBH). We manually write CoT exemplars for BBH.
